posture_summary.text: Chile's transition period concludes with strong validation of institutional and economic functionality as Kast prepares to assume office. The successful CODELCO bond issuance ($1.25B oversubscribed) and Supreme Court's definitive rejection of Chinese legal challenges to the lithium partnership demonstrate both market confidence and regulatory sovereignty over strategic minerals. The completion of Kast's technocratic cabinet structure (67% independent) confirms adaptation to congressional constraints, while continued judicial accountability processes (Vivanco corruption case) validate institutional independence. Kast's operational partnership-building with restrictive immigration models (Dominican Republic) persists despite logistical challenges, maintaining the alignment approach without broader strategic realignment. Chile enters the Kast era with demonstrated state capacity, market credibility, and institutional continuity.
